ai.description: The Kerala Warty Frog (Dicroglossidae) reaches 35–45 mm. It is brown with a distinct pale vertebral stripe and numerous prominent, longitudinal skin ridges. The throat is dark with a central white line.
ai.identificationRemarks: *Minervarya keralensis* is best distinguished by the presence of a distinct, continuous, and prominent glandular fold running along the sides of its back (dorsolateral fold).
ai.habitat: The Kerala Warty Frog inhabits leaf litter and moist ground within evergreen and semi-evergreen forests, typically at elevations between 200 and 1,200 meters.
ai.behavior: The Kerala Warty Frog is primarily nocturnal, emerging after dark to forage for small invertebrates among the leaf litter of forest floors and wetlands.
ai.reproductionNotes: *Minervarya keralensis* is an oviparous breeder that lays clutches of 200–500 eggs in temporary pools. Breeding occurs during the monsoon season, typically from June to August.
ai.distributionRemarks: *Minervarya keralensis* is endemic to the Western Ghats of India, primarily occurring in the states of Kerala and Tamil Nadu at elevations between 200 and 1,200 meters.
ai.callDescription: The Kerala Warty Frog produces a series of short, high-pitched "tink" notes, typically heard from shallow, rain-filled ditches or paddy fields during the monsoon.
